title.narrative: Supporting Climate and Disaster Resilience in Nepal (CDRIN)

description.narrative:
The goal of CDRIN is to build more resilient local economies and communities that can withstand the impact of climate change, promote sustainable development and contribute to the achievement of the Paris Agreement and localisation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
CDRIN end-of-program outcomes (EOPO) are: EOPO 1: Reduced risk of landslide hazards to minimise loss of lives and damage of properties in Nepal EOPO 2: Increased local government’s access to climate finance to implement climate change mitigation and adaptation investments in Nepal (UNCDF) EOPO 3: A standard and internationally recognised mechanism of performance-based climate resilience grants established and institutionalised in Nepal (UNCDF)

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: In partnership with Practical Action and government stakeholders, Australian funding is helping to strengthen landslide early warning systems for local communities in one of the most disaster-prone areas in Nepal. This program is developing rainfall thresholds for landslide detection, which will be integrated into Department of Hydrology and Meteorology’s forecasting. The partnership is reducing vulnerability to climatic and disaster risks for 2,135 people directly and 38,494 people indirectly in two municipalities in central Nepal.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Nirmala Dhital, 47, principal of Shree Ganesh Basic School in Tipeni, is a member of the early warning task force supported by the CDRIN program. Trained in early warning and risk communication, Nirmala played a key role during the landslide of 14 July 2024 that blocked Larke Khola and triggered a flood downstream. Upon receiving alerts from the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) and local authorities, Nirmala activated the alert system and was able to quickly inform all households using phone calls and a dedicated messaging group. Despite significant damage, her actions ensured a timely evacuation and prevented casualties. ‍ This success reflects the impact of community-led systems, early preparedness, and citizen science in disaster risk reduction and preparedness. Nirmala credits the training and support from Practical Action and DHM’s timely alerts for the effective response. Reflecting on her experience, Nirmala said, “In times of disaster, it is not just about having the right knowledge but the skills to act instantly. This shows the critical role of systems and community-led institutions in reducing disaster impacts.”

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Recognising landslides as a major climate hazard, the CDRIN project focused on strengthening community-centric early warning systems. This included the development of rainfall-induced landslide thresholds, which have been integrated into impact-based forecasting, and the establishment of automatic weather stations, supported by municipal funding to ensure their protection and incentives for use of gauge readers. This demonstrates Nepal’s readiness to use technology as an adaptation strategy to address landslide risks. The program hosted a national-level event to gather input and feedback for the final version of the National Framework on Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems, which integrated insights from the community-centric early warning systems into the Government of Nepal’s disaster management approach.
